reference.sections: PDF page 2, brief everyday exchanges around departures and casual greetings; consulted only for compact spoken turn-taking. A1 language limits come from the approved framework and published Mini Talks A1 001, not this higher-level source.
reference.rights: Reference-only copyrighted third-party material. No excerpt, characters, setting, plot or distinctive phrasing is adapted or quoted; all nine scenes, dialogues and Korean meanings are original TalkTag writing.
reference.conversion: Text-extracted private Markdown companion, with no unresolved pages in REFERENCE_MD_INDEX.md. The missing My Close Call index target, garbled action-expression OCR, profane HOOPS register and garbled Curious Incident OCR were not used.

practice.input: See a concrete scene, then hear one naturally paced two-person American-English exchange with optional script and Korean meaning; replay or shadow by learner choice.
practice.output: Recognize who needs what, summarize the exchange, and adapt one practical line to a nearby real-life need.
practice.dings: One start cue and one end cue per finished card

cards.title: One Roll, Please
cards.situation: A customer buys a plain bread roll at a neighborhood bakery counter.
cards.situationKo: 손님이 빵집에서 작은 빵 하나를 삽니다.
cards.descriptionKo: 빵집에서 먹고 싶은 빵을 고르고, 데울지 묻는 말에 답해요.
cards.learnerInput: A bread roll in the display case and a simple offer to warm it.
cards.expectedOutput: Order one item and answer a simple preparation question.
cards.artworkBrief: A customer points to a plain bread roll at the bakery counter; the clerk holds a small paper bag. No printed dialogue or prices in the image.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.en: Sure. Do you want it warm?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.en: Here you go. That's three dollars.

variationPrompt.en: The customer does not want the roll warmed. What could Ava say?
variationPrompt.ko: 손님이 빵을 데우지 않고 먹고 싶어요. 에이바라면 어떻게 말할까요?
variationPrompt.sampleAnswerHidden: No, thank you. It's fine as it is.

cards.title: Where's the Elevator?
cards.situation: A visitor asks a receptionist where to find the elevator in an office-building lobby.
cards.situationKo: 방문객이 건물 안내 데스크에서 엘리베이터 위치를 묻습니다.
cards.descriptionKo: 건물 안에서 엘리베이터를 찾아 짧은 길 안내를 들어요.
cards.learnerInput: An elevator visible just behind the office lobby desk.
cards.expectedOutput: Ask where the elevator is and check one direction.
cards.artworkBrief: A visitor speaks to a receptionist at a simple lobby desk; the receptionist points to the elevators behind her. No readable signs.

variationPrompt.en: The elevator is behind Joy, on the left. What could Joy say?
variationPrompt.ko: 엘리베이터가 조이 뒤쪽 왼편에 있어요. 조이라면 어떻게 알려 줄까요?
variationPrompt.sampleAnswerHidden: It's behind me, on the left.

cards.title: Is This Your Notebook?
cards.situation: A classmate finds a notebook under another student's chair before class.
cards.situationKo: 수업이 시작되기 전, 공책 하나가 의자 아래에서 나옵니다.
cards.descriptionKo: 친구가 찾던 공책을 발견하고 어디에 있었는지 알려 줘요.
cards.learnerInput: One notebook beneath a chair; the owner needs it for class.
cards.expectedOutput: Identify an object and say where it was found.
cards.artworkBrief: One classmate picks up a notebook from beneath the other classmate's chair before class; both look relieved. No names or writing on the cover.

lines.speaker: noah
lines.en: Thanks. I need it for class.

variationPrompt.en: The notebook is not Noah's. What could he say?
variationPrompt.ko: 그 공책이 노아의 것이 아니에요. 노아라면 어떻게 말할까요?

cards.title: Does This Bus Go Downtown?
cards.situation: A passenger asks the driver of a fictional city bus whether it goes downtown.
cards.situationKo: 버스가 정류장에 서자 승객이 기사에게 시내로 가는지 묻습니다.
cards.descriptionKo: 버스 기사에게 목적지를 확인하고 타도 되는지 물어요.
cards.learnerInput: A bus at a stop, with no real-world transit claim.
cards.expectedOutput: Check the destination and ask whether to board.
cards.artworkBrief: A passenger asks the driver of a fictional city bus at an open door. Avoid route numbers or real city details in the image.

lines.speaker: zoe
lines.en: Excuse me. Does this bus go downtown?

variationPrompt.en: The bus goes to the library, not downtown. What could Miles say?
variationPrompt.ko: 그 버스는 시내가 아니라 도서관으로 가요. 기사 마일스라면 어떻게 알려 줄까요?
variationPrompt.sampleAnswerHidden: No, this bus goes to the library.

cards.title: A Pen for the Form
cards.situation: A visitor borrows a pen to sign in at a community-center welcome desk.
cards.situationKo: 방문객이 커뮤니티 센터에 들러 이름을 적고 펜을 돌려줍니다.
cards.descriptionKo: 접수대에서 펜을 빌리고 이름을 어디에 적을지 물어요.
cards.learnerInput: A pen and a sign-in form with one blank name line.
cards.expectedOutput: Borrow a pen and confirm where to write a name.
cards.artworkBrief: A visitor fills in one line of a simple sign-in form with a borrowed pen; a volunteer stands behind the desk. The form is blank/unreadable in the illustration.

lines.speaker: grace
lines.en: Hi. Do you have a pen?
lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 펜 좀 빌릴 수 있을까요?

lines.speaker: grace
lines.en: Thanks. Do I write my name here?

variationPrompt.en: Grace also needs to write her phone number. What could she ask?
variationPrompt.ko: 그레이스가 전화번호도 적어야 해요. 어떻게 물으면 좋을까요?
variationPrompt.sampleAnswerHidden: Do I write my phone number here too?

cards.title: Can You Take a Photo?
cards.situation: A park visitor asks another person to take a photo by a tree.
cards.situationKo: 공원을 찾은 사람이 지나가던 사람에게 사진을 부탁합니다.
cards.descriptionKo: 공원에서 사진을 부탁하고 찍힌 사진을 확인해요.
cards.learnerInput: A tree and a phone that the visitor hands over for one photo.
cards.expectedOutput: Ask for a simple favor and check the result.
cards.artworkBrief: One visitor stands beside a tree while another holds the visitor's phone to take a picture. Show only the two speaking characters and no legible phone screen.

lines.speaker: lucy
lines.en: Excuse me. Can you take my photo?
lines.ko: 실례해요. 사진 한 장만 찍어 주실 수 있나요?

variationPrompt.en: Lucy wants a second photo. What could she ask?
variationPrompt.ko: 루시가 사진을 한 장 더 찍고 싶어요. 어떻게 부탁하면 좋을까요?
variationPrompt.sampleAnswerHidden: Could you take one more, please?

cards.title: Is This Machine Free?
cards.situation: One customer has just finished using a washer in a self-service laundromat.
cards.situationKo: 두 손님이 세탁기 앞에서 차례를 넘겨줍니다.
cards.descriptionKo: 빨래방에서 빈 세탁기를 확인하고 동전을 어디에 넣는지 물어요.
cards.learnerInput: An empty washer and a visible coin slot.
cards.expectedOutput: Check whether a machine is available and ask how to start it.
cards.artworkBrief: One customer closes an empty washer while another holds a small laundry basket and coins. No brand names, text, or detailed machine controls.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.en: Excuse me. Is this washer free?

variationPrompt.en: Nora has no coins. What could she ask Eli?
variationPrompt.ko: 노라에게 동전이 없어요. 엘리에게 어떻게 물으면 좋을까요?
variationPrompt.sampleAnswerHidden: Do you know where I can get coins?

cards.title: Can You Help with This Box?
cards.situation: A resident carrying a box asks a neighbor to help him take it up the apartment stairs.
cards.situationKo: 아파트 계단 앞에서 이웃이 무거운 상자를 함께 듭니다.
cards.descriptionKo: 상자를 옮기는 데 도움을 청하고 함께 들고 올라가요.
cards.learnerInput: One box at the foot of the apartment stairs.
cards.expectedOutput: Ask someone to help carry an object and give a simple destination.
cards.artworkBrief: A man carrying a box on apartment stairs asks a woman neighbor stepping toward him for help. No delivery logos or readable apartment numbers.

lines.speaker: mark
lines.en: Can you help me with this box?
lines.ko: 이 상자 좀 같이 들어주실 수 있어요?

variationPrompt.en: The box needs to go to the first floor. What could Mark say?
variationPrompt.ko: 상자를 1층으로 옮겨야 해요. 마크라면 어떻게 말할까요?
variationPrompt.sampleAnswerHidden: Just to the first floor, please.

cards.title: Are You Free Tonight?
cards.situation: Two friendly neighbors meet in their apartment courtyard at dusk and arrange dinner.
cards.situationKo: 저녁 무렵 아파트 안뜰에서 만난 이웃 둘이 함께 식사하기로 합니다.
cards.descriptionKo: 이웃을 저녁 식사에 초대하고 시간을 다시 확인해요.
cards.learnerInput: Two neighbors talking in an apartment courtyard before dinner at seven.
cards.expectedOutput: Invite someone to a simple meal and confirm the time.
cards.artworkBrief: Two neighbors talk in an apartment courtyard at dusk; one casually invites the other to dinner later. Other residents dine quietly in the background, but only the two foreground neighbors speak. No legible text.

lines.speaker: emma
lines.en: I'm making dinner at seven. Want to come over?
lines.ko: 7시에 저녁 만들 건데, 와서 같이 드실래요?

lines.speaker: dan
lines.en: That sounds nice. Can I bring something?

variationPrompt.en: Dan is busy tonight but free tomorrow. What could he say?
variationPrompt.ko: 댄은 오늘은 바쁘지만 내일은 시간이 있어요. 어떻게 대답하면 좋을까요?
variationPrompt.sampleAnswerHidden: I can't tonight. Are you free tomorrow?
